trust_decision.summary: Client decides whether a caller- or redirect-supplied request target may be serialized into the HTTP/1.1 request line; at the pinned commit write_request_line concatenates method, target and version with no CR/LF/control check, unlike the WebSocket handshake and header writer which apply fields::is_field_value.

landing_point.why: The summary names open_stream; ClientImpl::open_stream builds req.path from the raw caller path (no encode_path) and calls write_request_line, already checking its return value.

fix_sites.entry_point: detail::write_request_line, shared by ClientImpl::open_stream (Client::open_stream, httplib::stream::Get/Post/... at httplib.h:3518-3757) and ClientImpl::write_request

ClientImpl::write_request, reached by Client::Get/Post/.../send(Request) with set_path_encode(false), redirect following (httplib.h:13575, 13579) and the SSL proxy CONNECT request (httplib.h:16236-16242)
fix_sites.module_kind: main buffered client request path (caller must propagate the new error)

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: httplib.h:13821-13852 (ClientImpl::write_request: buffered send path, separate from open_stream)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The report names open_stream; on the normal send()/Get() path encode_path escapes CR/LF by default (httplib.h:5114-5115), and set_path_encode(false) is documented as 'sends paths as-is' for pre-encoded URLs (README.md:1308-1310), so a solver can argue the verb methods are a user opt-out and not affected. Fixing only inside write_request_line also looks complete, but write_request ignores its return value (httplib.h:13852) and keeps writing headers.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: With set_path_encode(false), pre-encoded targets including %0A, %00, %FF, %20 and '+' must be sent verbatim with no decoding or re-encoding; a fix that decodes before checking, or that forces encoding or normalisation on that path, breaks this. Spaces in paths are still encoded on the default path.

O6_input_shapes: CRLF CRLF followed by a full second request (request smuggling)
CR/LF from a percent-decoded redirect Location (%0D%0A) with set_path_encode(false)
other control octets rejected by is_field_value (e.g. NUL, which is not VCHAR)

O7_producer.where: httplib.h:13575 (ClientImpl::redirect percent-decodes the Location path with decode_path_component before re-sending)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: Method token in the same request line: write_request_line concatenates the caller-supplied method unchecked, and the published check validates only the path. Method is reachable through ClientImpl::open_stream(method, ...) and send(Request) with req.method.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The advisory says 'request target'; methods are usually programmer-chosen constants, not attacker data.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same function as the fix (httplib.h:7543-7550); public entry points at httplib.h:13150/13216 and httplib.h:13079

O8b_injection_room.sibling: WebSocket handshake builds its own request line; a copy that drops the path check at httplib.h:8972 (or validates only host) would be a second implementation.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: It already builds the request line separately from write_request_line, so a maintainer refactor could easily drop or narrow the guard.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: SSL proxy CONNECT target built from host_ via make_host_and_port_string_always_port; a variant that writes the CONNECT line directly instead of through process_request would bypass the new check.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: host_ can come from a redirect Location (httplib.h:13559, 13612), and proxy tunnelling code is often hand-rolled.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: is_field_value accepts interior SP/HTAB, so a target such as '/a HTTP/1.0' still passes the published check and yields an extra request-line token (a how-type parser differential on the target).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The fix reuses a header-value predicate for a request target whose grammar forbids SP.

O9_family: CWE-113 CRLF / HTTP request-line splitting (client-side request injection)

O10_build.language: C++ (C++11 header-only; candidate metadata says C)
O10_build.toolchain: g++/clang++ via test/Makefile, CMake or meson; bundled googletest in test/gtest; OpenSSL optional
O10_build.project_tests: test/test.cc PathUrlEncodeTest (test/test.cc:3060-3141), plus ServerResponseSplittingTest near the fix's test insertion point (fix.diff:76); tests use a loopback Server+Client

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Validate or encode the path inside ClientImpl::open_stream only (or add the check in write_request_line without making write_request honour the return value), leaving the set_path_encode(false)/redirect send path open or still emitting headers.

out_of_scope_notes: Redirect host from Location becomes the new client's host_ (httplib.h:13559, 13612, 13647); Host header values are validated by check_and_write_headers, so this was not pursued.
